reasoning: The belief that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short (around 5 feet 2 inches) is a historical misconception stemming from a confusion between French and British units of measurement, reinforced by contemporary British propaganda (such as caricatures by James Gillray). At the time of his autopsy, Napoleon was measured at 5 feet 2 inches in pre-metric French measurements (pieds and pouces). When converted to modern/English imperial units, his actual height was approximately 5 feet 6.5 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (around 169 cm). This made him average or slightly above average in height for a French man of the early 19th century.
